decorative_engine_tests.host_numpy_imported: NO in all three. jax.numpy is the JAX API, not host numpy. Julia uses QuantumOptics + LinearAlgebra. PyTorch imports only torch plus stdlib cmath for its cross-check.
decorative_engine_tests.file_reads: NONE. Every open() in all three sources is write-mode: jax:176, pytorch:204, julia:285. No json.load, no read(), no include() of another leg, no readchomp.
decorative_engine_tests.cross_leg_references: NONE. Each leg names only its own output filename, and only to write it. No leg can consume another leg's output.
decorative_engine_tests.copied_from_each_other: No. Distinct idiom per leg (jax @jit + jax.scipy expm; torch .mH + linalg.matrix_exp + explicit .contiguous() workaround; julia QuantumOptics.liouvillian + LinearAlgebra exp). Structure is parallel because the task is shared, not because text was copied.

overall_verdict: This round produced real evidence, and it also produced a headline that is broader than the evidence. The substrate result is genuine and survives adversarial probing: three engines, three languages, agreement at the floating-point floor on a problem with a known exact answer, with the engine calls demonstrably value-coupled. Against that, one specific favourable-sounding claim is false as stated -- the repo's own oracle gate exits 1 today and was reported as passing -- the blamed file is misidentified and unfixed, exit 0 was allowed to carry weight it cannot bear, and two different artifact sets were merged into a single sentence. Nothing in the round bears on manifold capability, and the repo's own report still records zero admitted manifold layers.
